# models.glycogen { #wdm.models.glycogen }

`models.glycogen`

Fast water compartments: glycogen-bound and sodium-associated water.

These two states exist to explain the difference between what you weigh and
what you *are*. Both respond within days to dietary inputs, both move the scale
by kilograms, and neither has anything to do with fat.

**Glycogen.** Stored carbohydrate is held with roughly three grams of water per
gram of glycogen. Total stores range over ~300-600 g, so a swing between
carbohydrate restriction and repletion moves 200 g of glycogen plus 600 g of
water: nearly a kilogram of scale weight with zero change in tissue. This single
mechanism explains the notorious first-week "success" of low-carbohydrate diets
and the equally notorious overnight "relapse" after one high-carbohydrate meal.

**Sodium.** Extracellular fluid volume tracks sodium load on a one-to-two day
timescale. Frequently a larger source of scale noise than carbohydrate, and
almost never logged, which is why an unlogged salty meal is the single most
common explanation for an inexplicable overnight gain.

Both are modeled as first-order lags toward an input-proportional steady state.
Deviations are measured from the subject's habitual (pre-diet) intake, the
episode's ``carb_ref_g``/``sodium_ref_mg`` (see `~wdm.io.Episode`), so a
diet that starts from ordinary eating starts both states at zero, and the drain
of glycogen water as carbohydrate drops is predicted rather than absorbed.

## Functions

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [glycogen_rate](#wdm.models.glycogen.glycogen_rate) | Time derivative of the glycogen-water compartment, kg/day. |
| [glycogen_steady_state](#wdm.models.glycogen.glycogen_steady_state) | Equilibrium glycogen-complex deviation for today's carbohydrate, kg. |
| [sodium_rate](#wdm.models.glycogen.sodium_rate) | Time derivative of the sodium-water compartment, kg/day. |
| [sodium_steady_state](#wdm.models.glycogen.sodium_steady_state) | Equilibrium sodium-associated water deviation, kg. |

### glycogen_rate { #wdm.models.glycogen.glycogen_rate }

```python
models.glycogen.glycogen_rate(x, u, p)
```

Time derivative of the glycogen-water compartment, kg/day.

### glycogen_steady_state { #wdm.models.glycogen.glycogen_steady_state }

```python
models.glycogen.glycogen_steady_state(u, p)
```

Equilibrium glycogen-complex deviation for today's carbohydrate, kg.

### sodium_rate { #wdm.models.glycogen.sodium_rate }

```python
models.glycogen.sodium_rate(x, u, p)
```

Time derivative of the sodium-water compartment, kg/day.

### sodium_steady_state { #wdm.models.glycogen.sodium_steady_state }

```python
models.glycogen.sodium_steady_state(u, p)
```

Equilibrium sodium-associated water deviation, kg.

Identically zero when no sodium column is supplied, since ``sodium_dev_mg``
is then zero for every day and the state decays to and stays at zero. The
compartment costs nothing when unused, which is why it is always present in
the state vector rather than switched in and out.
